campaign_name: PR-PLAY — System-Agnostic Object Observation and Disclosure Policy
purpose: Bounded internal production projection and information-boundary verification
executive_summary:
**A/PASS for bounded trusted internal object disclosure.**

88 observation tests passed; supplemental visibility/confidentiality/publication: 238 passed / 2 failed / 0 errors / 0 skipped (240 tests), identical failure identities/pass count with the new module import-blocked in a feature-absent control.

Combined before: 405 passed / 20 failed / 0 errors / 0 skipped (425 tests). After: 405 passed / 20 failed / 0 errors / 0 skipped (425 tests). New failures: []; newly passing: [].

inspection: 72 before / 72 after; marking: 76 before / 76 after; identity: 52 before / 52 after; inventory_snapshot: 50 before / 50 after; preservation: 143 before / 143 after.

One new production module, no existing production changes. Current active markings project through a reusable category contract and a single concrete marking adapter. Visible/concealed/restricted permissions are consumed, never adjudicated. Unknown legacy classification fails closed; ordinary empty visual results mean unknown, not absence. Hidden, removed, unrelated and private lineage data do not escape. Real save/reload and snapshots preserve permitted results. All twelve HTTP turns unchanged. Live provider calls: **0**.

Trusted internal Python entry only. No authenticated observation-decision issuer exists; the private typed grant is an upstream assertion, not cryptographic authentication or independent physical-feasibility verification. Caller must supply a coherent authoritative character snapshot under the existing read lane and reestablish grants when current visibility/access/scene evidence changes. Revision plus relevant-state fingerprint detect target changes, but the service does not independently load scene state, revoke rights or adjudicate reachability. Visibility metadata is consumed from authoritative object state; no classification authoring/migration API ships. Existing legacy markings therefore remain undisclosed until upstream establishes classification. No player route, natural-language observation, AI narration, T06 completion, mechanics, transfers or general-purpose property ontology. No full-suite, independent holdout, live-model or gameplay-improvement claim. Internal Python runtime is not a cryptographic constant-time boundary; no observer-facing timing, hidden counts, diagnostics, receipt traversal or public timing route is exposed.
